data.title: Trading on Margin: What It Means and How to Get Started
data.description:
Why trade Bitcoin if stocks can double? The leverage question traders miss

A trader recently asked: "Why trade Bitcoin? What's it gonna do, 2x, 3x? These days stocks can do that. So what's the point?"

It's a reasonable question, but it misses something fundamental about trading: leverage.

data.title: Record ETF Inflows, Yet Stock Market Leadership Is Shifting. What's Going On?
data.description:
Stock market sector rotation: Energy leads while communication services suffers a sharp decline

U.S. stock market leadership is becoming increasingly selective. Three trading sessions reveal important differences between sectors, and even between industries within the same sector.

U.S. stocks are showing a notable change in leadership. Between the October 20 and October 23, 2026 closes, the Energy Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLE) gained 2.00%, while the Communication Services Select Sector SPDR Fund (XLC) fell 4.25%. The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) declined 1.18% over the same period.

data.title: Dow leads stocks lower; small caps win the week
data.description:
The major U.S. stock indices closed lower on Friday, with the Dow industrial average leading the declines. The Nasdaq 100 came within a little more than one point of unchanged, but the performance underneath the surface was less encouraging.

Only six of the 30 Dow stocks advanced in the supplied breadth snapshot. Within the Nasdaq 100, declining stocks outnumbered advancing stocks by 67 to 33. Buyers were making a play in cybersecurity and selected software shares, but that buying did not extend across the market.

data.title: NZDUSD buyers are trying to make a play. The 38.2% retracement remains the next hurdle.
data.description:
The NZDUSD has moved higher on four of five trading days this week, giving buyers something to build on after a sharp decline from the August high. The recovery has included a failed break below the rising 100-hour moving average and two successful tests of that moving average today.

Those are encouraging developments for the buyers. They are starting to show up on dips and defend a technical level.

data.title: Earnings macro week ahead: The Fed and Big Tech report on the same day
data.description:
The Fed decision is Wednesday, October 28, but markets have mostly given up on a move: fed funds futures put the odds of a hold at roughly 90-92%. The market believes that a hike less than a week before the midterms would be politically awkward. So now the question isn’t really about a rate hike in the week ahead but December and that is now at 85% for a hike.

I will be watching macro data including Thursday's PCE report but I will also be looking for macro signals from companies reporting this week. Last week, we heard from airlines that continued to highlight strong travel demand and corporate spending in a good economic sign, but what abotut the rest of the economy? Housing is particularly interesting with interest rates high and a deep, ongoing recession in that sector.

data.title: US expected to remove 50% tariffs on some Canadian products as soon as today - report
data.description:
Election season is doing what trade negotiators couldn’t.

The Wall Street Journal reports the US is preparing to lift 50% tariffs on some Canadian agricultural and forestry products, with a proclamation possibly coming as soon as today. The motivation is political: Maine Sen. Susan Collins has been lobbying for relief and is in a dead heat with Democrat Troy Jackson with less than two weeks to go until Election Day.

data.title: Gold breaks below $4,000 target area before bouncing. What do buyers need to prove?
data.description:
In yesterday’s educational post, I discussed why gold was falling despite sharply lower Treasury yields. Lower yields would typically provide support for a non-interest-bearing asset like gold. However, the dollar was mixed, and gold’s inability to reclaim its hourly moving averages kept the technical bias tilted toward the sellers. The fundamental expectation needed confirmation from the price action. It did not get it.

Today, that technical story continued with a break below $4,000 before buyers finally pushed back.

data.title: US S&P Global flash October services PMI 57.9 vs 58.0 expected
data.description:
• Prior was 59.8
  • Manufacturing 56.0 vs 55.5 expected
  • Prior manufacturing 57.0
  • Composite 57.6 vs 58.4 prior
  • selling prices rose at the sharpest rate since August 2022
  • New orders highest in over four-and-a-half years
  • Business output expectations for the 12 months ahead cooled compared to September but were still the second highest seen this year

One of the big surprises last month -- and one that the market took as a hawkish signal at time time -- was the jump in this survey. Employment was at the strongest since June 2022 and input cost inflation at the highest since Oct 2022.
